text: {"known":[{"name":"Partial RoPE (rotate only a fraction of dims)","mechanism":"Apply rotary to only a small slice of each head's dimensions and leave the rest position-free.","effect":"Rotating about 10% of dims converges close to full RoPE, with up to 10x RoPE-cache savings. RoPE on only 2 channels (4%) or none ends at higher final loss. NoPE runs were sometimes unstable, and minimal RoPE or QK-Norm fixed that, though QK-Norm alone converged to a higher loss.","where":"Sequence lengths 1024, 4096 and 8192, several datasets and model sizes (Khan et al. 2026)","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.11611"},{"name":"LeRoPE: learnable per-frequency RoPE","mechanism":"Learn one scalar per rotary frequency instead of using a fixed geometric sequence from base theta.","effect":"Beats both RoPE and partial RoPE at every scale. At the largest scale RoPE needs 3.4% more FLOPs to match it. A high-norm positional band emerges in the learned frequencies.","where":"52M to 2.5B parameters, trained from scratch","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10134"},{"name":"Partial RoPE (50% of head dims) in modded-nanoGPT","mechanism":"Rotate half the head dims. The long sliding windows attend mostly to the unrotated (stationary) dims.","effect":"Used in the late-2025 speedrun records. The write-up says the long windows mostly use the unrotated dims, which helps window extension. I found no isolated ablation numbers.","where":"modded-nanoGPT, GPT-2-small-scale speedrun","url":"https://www.greaterwrong.com/posts/j3gp8tebQiFJqzBgg/how-the-nanogpt-speedrun-wr-dropped-by-20-in-3-months"},{"name":"QK-Norm in the speedrun recipe","mechanism":"RMS-normalize queries and keys before the dot product.","effect":"Part of the 15.2-minute record, alongside padded embeddings, ReLU², and zero-init projections. No separate ablation figure was given.","where":"modded-nanoGPT, GPT-2-small scale","url":"https://github.com/KellerJordan/modded-nanogpt"},{"name":"Partial RoPE with layer-wise LN scale (Parameter Golf)","mechanism":"Rotate only part of q and k, typically the first half, so the remaining dims learn position-agnostic features. It was paired with layer-wise LayerNorm scaling.","effect":"Submission #4 reached 1.1248 BPB. The page gives no separate ablation and does not isolate partial RoPE's contribution.","where":"OpenAI Parameter Golf, tiny-model leaderboard","url":"https://www.codesota.com/parameter-golf/architecture-tricks"},{"name":"QKNorm with a learnable scale g","mechanism":"L2-normalize q and k, then multiply the logits by a learnable scalar g instead of dividing by sqrt(d).","effect":"Average gain of 0.928 BLEU on five low-resource translation pairs. A 2026 follow-up generalizes it to an Lp norm and keeps a learnable positive scale alpha.","where":"Small translation models (TED Talks, IWSLT'15)","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.04245"},{"name":"Scalable-Softmax (SSMax)","mechanism":"Scale the logits by s·log n, with a learnable s, so that attention does not flatten as context n grows.","effect":"The abstract reports faster loss reduction in pretraining and clearly better long-context and key-retrieval performance. I did not read the paper's tables.","where":"Pretraining experiments in the paper; sizes not checked","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.19399"},{"name":"Head-specific sigmoid output gate after SDPA","mechanism":"A query-dependent sigmoid gate on the attention output adds non-linearity and sparsity.","effect":"Improves quality and reduces massive activations and attention sinks. It also helps long-context extrapolation.","where":"30 variants of 15B MoE and 1.7B dense models, 3.5T tokens (Qwen)","url":"https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/904e89bb4e632e75fb47f093b620b257-Abstract-Conference.html"},{"name":"Slowing upper-layer Q/K learning early in training","mechanism":"Temporarily lower the learning rate on only the upper-layer query/key projections so attention does not sharpen before lower-layer features stabilize.","effect":"Improves final perplexity and downstream accuracy. It is nearly unnecessary in LLaMA-style blocks, because gated FFNs are what suppress upstream residual writes.","where":"GPT-style pretraining (2026 preprint); sizes not checked","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10504"}],"failed":[{"name":"Learnable per-head sink logit (GPT-OSS style)","why":"MiniMax Sparse Attention found no clear or consistent perplexity gain, and the first token still acted as the sink, so they left it out. A separate paper reports that the sink-logit gain is largest at 10M parameters and shrinks by 124M, so it may not transfer to larger models.","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.13392"},{"name":"QK-Norm as the only positional or stability fix","why":"In the partial-RoPE study, NoPE with QK-Norm still converged to a higher loss than runs with 10% or more RoPE. QK-Norm stabilizes training but does not replace positional information.","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.11611"},{"name":"Learned per-token temperature without clipping","why":"A 2025 paper reports that the temperature drifts far from baseline and degrades performance, so it has to be clipped to a fixed range.","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2310.12956"}],"open":[{"direction":"Learnable or per-layer/per-head temperature (QK gain) on top of QK-RMSNorm, possibly with an log n term","why":"The fixed 1/sqrt(96) scale ignores layers where max logits reach 22.7 and entropy falls to 0.67. SSMax and QKNorm's learnable g motivate a test, but I found no small-scale ablation against a fixed scale in an MLA-style model.","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.19399"},{"direction":"Per-layer or learned rotary frequencies and theta, including the width of the rotary key","why":"LeRoPE finds a learned high-norm positional band at 52M to 2.5B parameters. The partial-RoPE study finds a 4% slice too small and 10% enough. I found no MLA-specific sweep of the decoupled-RoPE dimension count trained from scratch.","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10134"},{"direction":"NoPE and RoPE layer interleaving, with RoPE concentrated in early layers","why":"RNoPE-style alternation helps very long-context retrieval, and RoPE is said to matter most in early layers. I found no result at a 1024 context and 21M parameters.","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.21487"},{"direction":"Output gate on attention, as a replacement for a sink","why":"The gate removes sinks and massive activations in Qwen-scale models. I found no sub-100M ablation combined with decoupled RoPE and QK-norm.","url":"https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/904e89bb4e632e75fb47f093b620b257-Abstract-Conference.html"},{"direction":"Decoupled-RoPE dimension ablation inside MLA","why":"The DeepSeek review notes that no ablation of the decoupled RoPE has been reported. The only dimension sweep I found, 4 vs 8 dims on SmolLM-135M, converted a pretrained model and did not train MLA from scratch.","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2503.11486"}],"queries":["decoupled RoPE MLA partial rotary dimensions ablation small model","QK-norm learnable temperature attention scale softmax logit growth entropy collapse","modded-nanogpt speedrun record log partial key offset QK norm RoPE half-truncate attention","NoPE layers interleaved RoPE per-layer rope theta attention sink learned softmax scaling length 2025","Gated attention for LLMs non-linearity sparsity attention-sink-free Qwen","Scalable-Softmax Is Superior for Attention log n scaling","Query-Key Normalization for Transformers learnable scale g","Khan 2026 partial RoPE 10% dimensions training dynamics convergence rotary","attention sink learned sink logit softmax-off-by-one gpt-oss small model pretraining ablation"]}
